text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Insurer Aegon posts 18.5 pct rise in 1996 net to Dfl 156 bn, surpassing own forecast of 16.5 pct increase. (p1)
- First Dutch case of mad cow disease discovered at dairy farm in Overijssel province. (p1)
- Philips Electronics strongly divided on strategy of 82 pct-owned software subsidiary Origin. (p1)
- State-owned Dutch Rail NS lifts 1996 net by seven pct, due to lower extraordinary charges, costs and taxes. (p1)
- Economic affairs minister Hans Wijers to probe why virtually all petrol sales in the Netherlands controlled by traditional oil companies. (p3)
- Dutch accountancy association NOvAA loses court case against economics minister over his refusal to allow a raise in contribution to finance an advertising campaign. (p3)
- ABN Amro bank consider taking over London-based asset manager Capel Cure Myers. (p4)
- Rabobank sets up joint venture for foreign exchange research with Swiss software and research firm Olsen & associates. (p13)
VOLKSKRANT
- One man killed in battle between footbal hooligans. (p1)
- Mad cow disease discovered last Friday possibly caused by concentrate feed. (p1)
- Associated British Foods (ABF) eyeing Unilever's chemicals division. (p2)
- Chips tester for the computer industry Rood Testhouse's 1996 profit drops to Dfl 162,000 from 1995. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- D 66 party wants economic affairs minister Hans Wijers to head the list of candidates for next year's election. (p1)
- Dutch transport sector to lose 120 million guilders a year by French ban on truckers driving on Sundays. (p4)
- Dutch foreign affairs ministry calls on people to leave Zaire. (p6)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM objects to U.S. partner Northwest Airlines intended alliance with Australia's Qantas. (p13)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Agricultural minister Jozias van Aartsen wants pigs with computer chips to control spreading of swine fever. (p11)
TROUW
- Politics calls for tougher anti-hooligan measures. (p1)
